text: Two families of organic halogen compounds contain a benzene ring. In a haloarene, or aryl halide, the halogen sits directly on a ring carbon, like chlorobenzene. In an aralkyl halide, like benzyl chloride, it sits on the side chain. The two behave completely differently.
